claims.statement: The repository's CI workflow runs on pushes to `main` and `dev` and on every pull request, and defines exactly two jobs: the `lint-test-license` gate job and `fresh-install`.

The steps of the `lint-test-license` job are exactly the commands the governance docs require before a change is done (sync dev extras, ruff, version consistency, pytest, license scan, preflight scan), so a local pass and a CI pass are the same event.

The CI gate environment installs only the `dev` extra, so the `sidecar` and `bench` extras are absent from CI, and optional-dependency code paths therefore import their heavy libraries lazily and are exercised in the suite with injected fake extractors.
`ruff` is configured with `select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]` at line length 100, and pytest is configured with `--import-mode=importlib` over the `tests/` path, in `pyproject.toml`.

Test determinism comes from two shared fixtures: `FakeEmbedder` hashes text into a unit vector of exactly `EMBED_DIM` floats so identical text maps to an identical vector and rebuilds are reproducible, and `make_corpus` builds a small markdown repository that is optionally git-initialized with a deterministic commit; `conftest.py` also puts `harness/` on `sys.path` so the suite can import tools that are not part of the installed package.

The test suite is offline because the embedding credential is neutralized rather than mocked away: tests delete `OPENAI_API_KEY` and repoint `config._DOTENV_PATHS` at a nonexistent path, so dense retrieval degrades to lexical-only and assertions check that degradation, while a separate test asserts the fail-loud missing-key path of `embed.smoke_embed_or_die()`.
The repository is test-first: no new production behavior without a failing test first, and a red test is either fixed in the change or filed as a tracked issue, never dismissed or deleted.

The test suite dominates the local gate loop's wall-clock time (recorded as about 3 minutes on a fresh Linux runner and roughly 15 minutes for ~750 tests in the cloud dev VM) and is git-subprocess and index-I/O bound with low CPU, so a long quiet run must not be mistaken for a hang and killed.

The version-consistency gate treats `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` as the single authority and fails when the in-package `__version__`, any plugin manifest version slot (including nested `plugins[].version` entries) or existing citation metadata disagrees, reporting a manifest with no version slot as a problem and naming the diverging file and both versions in the failure message.

The version gate asserts consistency in CI instead of deriving the manifests at build time — recorded in the script as the chosen lowest-churn default, with manifest generation noted as a drop-in replacement if preferred later.

The license gate fails on strong-copyleft license strings (AGPL, GPL, SSPL) in the resolved environment, reports LGPL informationally rather than failing, does not deny a dependency whose metadata declares no license or `UNKNOWN`, and reads licenses from `pip-licenses --format=json --with-system` with an `importlib.metadata` fallback when that tool is absent.

The license gate is dependency-scoped: it excludes the project's own distribution before classification, keyed on the PEP 503-normalized `[project].name`, because `uv sync` installs the root project into the environment — so the engine's own `AGPL-3.0-only` license cannot make the gate reject the project, while the exclusion keys on the name only and a real copyleft dependency is still denied.

The preflight public scan inspects only `git ls-files`-tracked paths and skips binary or unreadable files, always excludes `docs/launch/` plus its own script and test, and in default mode scans non-docs files and the durable docs while deferring inherited process-history documents and reporting how many it deferred instead of dropping them silently.

The preflight scan's `--strict` mode scans all tracked docs including `docs/archive/`, so archiving a document can never hide a leak from the flip-time gate, and its separate history scan over commit diffs is informational only and never fails the run.
Preflight findings print the file, line, pattern label and a masked (truncated) match value, so the gate never re-prints the matched secret into a console or CI log.

The preflight deny set targets specific operator identifiers and credential shapes rather than generic categories: the shared CGNAT documentation range and empty `VAR=` placeholders are deliberately clean, which is why committed docs, fixtures and media assets must use placeholders instead of real operator values.

Each gate script is itself under test: offline tests load the script by path with `importlib`, assert the real tree passes, and assert planted failures are detected (diverging manifest, planted copyleft dependency, planted operator secret, missing or empty changelog section).

The `fresh-install` CI job builds the sdist and wheel, installs the wheel into a clean virtualenv resolved from PyPI with no lockfile, prints the resolved runtime dependencies, then proves the package starts by importing `mcp_server`, printing the version and rendering `serve --help`; it exists because `uv.lock` does not travel with the published distributions, so no lock-resolved job can see a dependency resolving to a breaking major (the LS-2550 `mcp` 2.0.0 crash-loop).

`tests/test_dependency_bounds.py` is the cheap local half of the fresh-install protection: every `[project].dependencies` entry must carry an upper bound (`<`, `~=`, `==`, or `.*`) while optional extras may float, and a second test requires `mcp<2` while `mcp_server.py` imports `mcp.server.fastmcp`, skipping with a note to revisit the bound if that import ever disappears.

Branch topology: `dev` is the default branch and the baseline for all work, feature and fix branches PR into `dev`, `main` is the release branch that receives only `dev` and never a feature branch, direct commits to either branch are forbidden, and divergence is reconciled by merging `main` back into `dev` rather than cherry-picking.
Commits use conventional subjects and require a DCO `Signed-off-by:` line (`git commit -s`), and a contributor licence agreement is deliberately not required.
Only a `v*.*.*` tag push or a manual `workflow_dispatch` triggers the release workflow, so merging to `main` runs CI and publishes nothing.

The release workflow is three dependent jobs: `build` re-runs the version-consistency gate, runs `uv build` and uploads the `dist` artifact with `if-no-files-found: error`; `publish` needs `build` and uploads via `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` under the `pypi` environment using OIDC trusted publishing with `id-token: write` and no stored API token; `github-release` needs `publish`, runs only for `refs/tags/v`, and is the only job with `contents: write`, the others staying read-only.
Because only the `github-release` job is guarded by the tag ref, a manual `workflow_dispatch` publishes to PyPI without creating a GitHub release.

Publishing depends on one-time operator setup of a PyPI trusted publisher naming the owner, repository, workflow and the `pypi` environment, which must match the `environment:` declared in the publish job.

GitHub release notes are derived from `CHANGELOG.md` by `scripts/changelog_section.py`, which refuses `[Unreleased]` and exits non-zero when the requested section is missing or empty; the job prepends an install/PyPI/full-changelog line, appends a compare link to the previous tag located with `git describe` (hence the `fetch-depth: 0` checkout), and creates the release with `--verify-tag` and the built `dist/*` artifacts attached.

Release prep runs in order: choose the number from the accumulated `[Unreleased]` section (a minor bump for new backwards-compatible functionality, patch for fixes only), bump `pyproject.toml` and let the version gate name the mirrored slots, cut `[Unreleased]` into a dated `[X.Y.Z]` section with a fresh empty `[Unreleased]` and updated compare links, promote `dev` to `main` by pull request, then tag `vX.Y.Z` on `main` at the exact commit to ship.

The changelog heading date and the citation files' `date-released` must equal the date the tag is actually pushed, and because the version-consistency gate checks versions only and not dates, this invariant is maintained manually.

Documentation is part of the change: a change is not done until every document it affects is corrected in the same pull request, a doc-sync table maps each changed surface to the documents that must move (including release-workflow or branch-topology changes updating both `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`), and the anti-drift rule is to reference the enforcing gate instead of copying its enumerable list, with `docs/README.md` current-truth pins overriding process-history documents.

Changes to auth, the MCP server, the write path or the protected-path/governance guard are security-sensitive and routed to the owner through `.github/CODEOWNERS`, which also covers the gate scripts and `/.github/` itself, and the pull request template carries the gate and security-surface checklists.

Operability is gated separately from retrieval quality: `scripts/product_smoke.py` runs a deterministic seven-stage loop on a disposable fixture vault with path-relative, secret-free output and is exercised in-process by the suite, and the first-class product readiness checklist is release-blocking with per-row recorded result, pass/fail, reviewer and date — pinned by `tests/test_product_readiness_docs.py`, which also requires that benchmark evidence stays separated from product proof.

`tests/test_changelog_section.py` also asserts that the real `CHANGELOG.md` already contains a section for the version declared in `pyproject.toml`, so the extraction gate behind the release notes is checked against the repository before release time.
